note: Tuberville (R) beats Doug Jones about 52-48 (AP call Nov. 4). Dems flip 2 House seats, incl. HD15, and 2 Senate seats (SD2, SD7); an independent narrowly takes a third GOP Senate seat (GOP 74-31 House, 24-10-1 Senate). GOP keeps both supermajorities. Independent Battles (SD10) leads by 72-74 votes and was sworn in Nov. 10; canvass is Nov. 13 and an automatic recount (margin under 0.5%) follows. The SD10 result doesn't change control or the supermajority (Alabama Political Reporter, Nov. 4 and 11; Fox10, Nov. 5).

Kreiss-Tomkins (D) leads Wilson (R) 49.9% to 28.8% on first choices and remains uncalled. He wins 56-44 in FairVote's preliminary ranked-choice tally; RCV tabulation is Nov. 18 and certification Nov. 25 (Alaska Watchman, Nov. 11; AP, Nov. 11). Coalitions named leaders and look set to keep both chambers, though AP still listed both undecided. Dems lead 2 GOP House seats (HD15, HD18) and independent Edgmon's open HD37; independents lead 2 GOP seats (HD5, HD34). In the Senate, independent Edgmon leads for Dem Lyman Hoffman's open SD S (ADN, Nov. 10-11).

Hobbs (D) reelected. AP called both chambers for Dems Nov. 6, the first Dem trifecta since 1966. Dems win 20 of 30 Senate seats (from 13), exactly the two-thirds needed to override, and are on track for 37 of 60 House seats (from 27), short of 40 (KTAR, Nov. 9; KJZZ, Nov. 6).

Sanders (R) reelected with about 54%. Dems gain 10 House seats (to 30 of 100), ending the GOP's three-fourths appropriations supermajority (75 votes) for the first time in a decade, though the GOP stays above two-thirds. Dem Allison Grigsby Sweatman flips SD13, 53-47 (Talk Business & Politics, Nov. 5; KJNB, Nov. 6; UA Little Rock Public Radio, Nov. 4).

Becerra (D) wins governor 64-36. Dems are on track to flip 6 GOP Assembly seats: AD36, AD47 and AD58 called by AP; Ta (AD70) conceded; Dems lead in AD7 and AD74. AD72 (R +111 votes) and AD33 are still close. In the Senate, Dems flip SD40 and SD36 (Strickland conceded Nov. 10), while SD6 Niello (R) leads by about 2 pts. Dems keep both supermajorities; counties report by Dec. 4 and the state certifies Dec. 11 (KCRA, Nov. 10; Voice of OC, Nov. 10; CSBA, Nov. 11).

Weiser (D) elected governor. Dems win two-thirds supermajorities in both chambers for the first time, flipping 6 House seats (HD15, 16, 19, 21, 50, 51) for 49 of 65 and SD30, where Leung beat Sen. Carson, for 24 of 35. HD21 and HD51 are about 51-49 but outside the 0.5% automatic-recount range, and the House supermajority holds even if both flip back. County canvass ends Nov. 25 and any recounts finish Dec. 4 (Colorado Politics, Nov. 9; Rocky Mountain Voice, Nov. 4).

Lamont (D) reelected. Dems flip 14 GOP House seats for 116-35 (unofficial; 3 House races went to automatic recounts, 2 conceded by Nov. 10). They flip 8 GOP Senate seats for a record 33-3, incl. SD34, where Mandato leads Sen. Cicarella by 259 votes after the Wallingford discrepancy recount; the district-wide recount was due Nov. 10. Dems keep both supermajorities (CTData, Nov. 9; Patch, Nov. 9; CT Mirror, Nov. 4).

Gov. Meyer (D) not up. Dems flip 3 GOP House seats (HD4 Long Neck, HD9 Middletown, HD34 Camden, where Norman beat Rep. Yearick by about 150 votes) for 30-11, reaching two-thirds in both chambers. The Senate is unchanged at 15-6 after Dems failed to flip GOP-held SD15 (Spotlight Delaware, Nov. 4; WHYY, Nov. 5).

Donalds (R) beats Jolly (D) 50.0-48.7. GOP loses supermajorities in both chambers: Dems win 50 of 120 House seats (+16) after McDow (D) takes HD33 by 286 votes in a machine recount (CF Public, Nov. 10), and net 1 Senate seat (Lowndes unseats Sen. Brodeur), leaving the GOP at 25, below the 27 needed (Ballotpedia).

Bottoms (D) beats Jackson (R) 54.3-45.7, a Dem flip with no runoff, and Dems win the House for the first time since 2004: 92 of 180 (from 81) per AJC (Nov. 6), counting a 27-vote Dem lead in a Lawrenceville seat; HD151 goes to a Dec. 1 runoff. GOP keeps the Senate; the +4 Senate figure was not reconfirmed this pass (AP via Yahoo, Nov. 12; Ballotpedia).

Gov. Josh Green (D) re-elected 71-27%. The GOP lost 4 of its 10 House seats: Dems flipped HD18, HD32 and HD39 (Pierick's open seat), and Green Party candidate Pa'ele Kiakona ousted Cochran in HD14 by 119 votes over the Democrat. That makes it 44 D-6 R-1 G, Dem +3. No Senate seats changed hands (State of Hawaii final printout, Nov. 10; Star-Advertiser, Nov. 6).

Gov. Brad Little (R) won a third term (AP). Dems flipped 6 seats in Boise (LD15), the Magic Valley (LD26) and Pocatello (LD29), going from 15 to 21 of 105 seats: House +5, Senate +1. The GOP keeps both supermajorities. Results are unofficial until the state canvass on Nov. 24 (Idaho Capital Sun, Nov. 4).

Pritzker (D) won a third term. Dems expand their 3/5 supermajorities to about 84-34 in the House (Capitol News Illinois projects 84 or 85) and 45-14 in the Senate. Sen. Syverson (R, SD35) and Rep. Keicher (R, HD70) still led narrowly with no call as of Nov. 9 (Capitol Fax). Counting deadline is Nov. 17.

Dems gain 16 House seats (54 R-46 D) and break the GOP's 2/3 supermajority, the largest House flip since 1974. Speaker Huston lost his seat, and Ben Smaltz is speaker-elect. In the Senate, Dems gain 5 and the GOP keeps its supermajority at 35-15 (Indiana Capital Chronicle, Nov. 9). Senate GOP leader Chris Garten leads Nick Marshall (D) by 297 votes in SD45, and Dems are weighing a recount. The candidate filing deadline is Nov. 17 (Indiana Capital Chronicle, Nov. 11). A Marshall win would make it 34-16, still a 2/3 majority.

Rob Sand (D) flips the governorship (AP). Dems flip 11 House seats without losing any (56 R-44 D), ending the GOP's House supermajority. In the Senate, Dems net +1 to 32-18: they flipped SD21 and SD47 (Wagle by 151 votes, no recount expected) and lost SD35 (Iowa Public Radio, Nov. 5; Bleeding Heartland, Nov. 6). The GOP has not held a Senate supermajority since a 2025 special election.

Holscher (D) leads Masterson 50.3% to 49.7% (7,000+ votes) and has declared victory, but the race is uncalled pending close-race audits (KWCH, Nov. 9). The state canvass is Nov. 16 and the recount request deadline 5 p.m. Nov. 17. The 0.5% state-paid recount threshold is narrowly not met. Dems flip as many as 20 House seats (68 R-57 D), breaking the GOP supermajority. Three House races are under audit: HD27 (Kiewiet D +41), HD40 (Buehler R +67) and HD117 (Holland D +133) (Kansas Reflector, Nov. 5). The Senate (31-9 GOP supermajority) was not up.

Dems flip 9 GOP seats (7 House, 2 Senate), including Majority Whip Nemes (by about 500 votes) and Sen. Raque Adams. The GOP took the open HD95 in Eastern Kentucky, so the House goes 74 R-26 D (Dem +6) and the Senate 30 R-8 D (Dem +2). The GOP keeps both supermajorities (KACo, Nov. 5; Louisville Public Media).

No legislative or governor election in 2026; the legislature and Gov. Landry (R) are next up in Oct./Nov. 2027. The GOP holds 2/3 in both chambers (House 71 of 105, needs 70; Senate 28 of 39, needs 26) (Ballotpedia).

Hannah Pingree (D) won governor (AP). Dems reach about 87 House seats (+12) and 24 of 35 Senate seats (+4), which would be the first Democratic 2/3 Senate supermajority since 1985. The 24th seat depends on SD18, where Bosworth (D) beat Andrews (R) by 50 votes, close enough for a state-funded recount. AP still had 1 Senate and 2 House races uncalled on Nov. 10 (Press Herald, Nov. 6; WABI, Nov. 10).

Gov. Wes Moore (D) re-elected by about 29 points. Mail ballots added Dem gains: Lara Westdorp ousted Sen. Bill Folden (R-Frederick) by 897 votes, making the Senate 35-12. Dems appear to flip 4 House seats (33B, 38B and two in District 4) (Maryland Matters, Nov. 7; Baltimore Banner, Nov. 7). Counties certify by Nov. 13, the state by Dec. 3.

Healey (D) reelected. Dems flipped 4 GOP House seats (3rd Barnstable, 22nd Middlesex, 20th Middlesex, 1st Worcester) and lost 8th Bristol to Jesse St. Gelais (R). Net Dem +3, or +4 if Hewins holds. The GOP caucus falls from 25 to 21 or 22 depending on 2nd Plymouth, where Hewins (D) leads Rep. Gaskey (R) by roughly 68-89 votes on shifting, unverified counts; recount petitions are due to the SOS Nov. 18, which is also the earliest certification date. The Senate is unchanged at 35-5 (State House News Service, Nov. 9-10; CommonWealth Beacon, Nov. 10).

Benson (D) elected governor; Democrats win a trifecta. Dems flip the House 63-47 (from 52-58), winning all 23 Ballotpedia battleground districts (11 R-to-D flips), and widen the Senate to 23-15 (from 20-18) by flipping SD9, SD30 and SD32 (Ballotpedia News, Nov. 8; Michigan Public, Nov. 5). Results are unofficial pending canvass.

Klobuchar (D) elected; DFL trifecta. DFL wins the House 77-57 (from a 67-67 tie) and widens the Senate to 39-28 (from 34-33); both majorities hold regardless of recounts. Recounts are pending in HD32A (West-R +22), SD4 (Peterson-R +4 over DFL Sen. Kupec) and SD33 (Housley-R +42); the state canvass is Nov. 19, and SD4's recount is likely Nov. 23-24 (KSTP, Nov. 11; KFGO, Nov. 10).

No legislative or gubernatorial elections in 2026 (next in 2027; Gov. Reeves (R)). The GOP lacks a veto-proof House majority (77 of 122; 82 needed). Dems broke the GOP Senate supermajority in Nov. 2025 court-ordered special elections, leaving 34 of 52 (35 needed) (Ballotpedia; Mississippi Free Press, Nov. 5, 2025).

The GOP loses the supermajorities it had held in both chambers since 2012. Dems flip 16 House seats (95-68; 109 needed for two-thirds) and 2 Senate seats, Fogle in Greene County and Ingle, who unseated Speaker Patterson in Jackson County, leaving the Senate at 22-12 (23 needed) (Missouri Independent/KCUR, Nov. 4 and 6). The closest flip, HD60 (Luther-D by 189 votes, 50.7%), is outside Missouri's 0.5% recount margin.

Dems flip HD4 (Koch) and HD20 (Keller, by about 46 votes) in the House (56-44) and SD10 (Mitchell) and SD29 (Rosenzweig) in the Senate (30-20); Republicans keep both chambers. HD48 stayed R by 32 votes (KTVH; Flathead Beacon, Nov. 8). Gov. Gianforte (R) is not up.

Pillen (R) reelected (AP call early Nov. 4; about 51-42 over Walz). The GOP loses its 33-seat filibuster-proof bloc, falling to 30. Dems pick up LD12 (Knorr defeats Riepe), LD18 (Goldoni, open R seat) and LD8 (Feichtinger, Hunt's independent seat), and independent Maxwell-Ostdiek beats Sen. von Gillern (R) in LD4 by 370 votes; von Gillern conceded Nov. 6. All trailing candidates have conceded, and the state canvass is in early December (Nebraska Examiner/Yahoo, Nov. 6; WOWT, Nov. 4).

Ford (D) unseats Gov. Lombardo. Dems flip 5 Assembly seats (AD2, 4, 13, 22, 35) for a 32-10 two-thirds supermajority (28 needed). AD22 is the closest: Booth (D) leads Hardy (R) by about 77 votes, called Nov. 10 but not yet canvassed. The Senate stays 13-8, one short of two-thirds, after Republicans held SD16 (+5,831) and SD20 (+9,492) (Nevada Independent, Nov. 10).

Ayotte (R) reelected; Dems flip both chambers. In the House, the clerk's prelim count is 291 D-108 R-1 I (Dems from 177 per NH Bulletin; Ballotpedia shows 169 seated plus vacancies), a two-thirds majority (267 needed) with 16 recounts underway through about Nov. 24 (NH Bulletin/Boston Globe, Nov. 11). The Senate is 15-9 D (from 8-16), one short of two-thirds, so the GOP's 16-8 Senate supermajority ends; no Senate recounts were sought, and Trumble lost SD8 by 389 (Keene Sentinel, Nov. 6).

No legislative or gubernatorial elections in 2026; Gov. Sherrill (D) took office Jan. 2026. Dems hold a two-thirds Assembly majority (57 of 80; 54 needed), and the Senate is 25-15 (27 needed). The next legislative elections are in Nov. 2027 (Ballotpedia).

Haaland (D) beat Hull (R) (AP via Scripps, Nov. 3). Dems flip 4 GOP House seats and lose 1 (HD4), reaching 47 of 70, exactly the 2/3 needed to override a veto. The ABQ Journal headline says Dems 'win supermajority,' but its text says close races were still pending and HD31 went narrowly to Chavez (R). Results are unofficial (ABQ Journal, Nov. 3-4; MultiState).

Hochul (D) reelected by about 20 points. Senate Dems regain their 2/3 supermajority: 45 seats were already called by Nov. 6 (42 needed), and they are on track for 47 of 63, with SD43 (Ashby-R vs. Lander-D) within a few hundred votes. The Assembly supermajority holds, with about 111 of 150 expected (+8 net, despite losing AD119) (City & State Nov. 4; NY1 Nov. 6; Greenberg Traurig Nov. 4).

Dems win the House for the first time since 2010, 71 of 120 (up from 47). They keep the majority even if they lose all 5 leads inside the 1% recount range (HDs 9, 20, 62, 63, 93). Senate control turns on SD24, where Britt (R) leads Hamm (D) by 228 votes (0.41%) after provisional ballots. If Britt holds, the GOP keeps 26-24; if not, it is 25-25 with Lt. Gov. Hunt (D) breaking ties. The GOP loses its Senate supermajority either way. Canvass Nov. 13; recount requests due Nov. 17 at noon; state certification Nov. 24 (NC Political News Nov. 11; WRAL Nov. 7; Carolina Journal Nov. 4).

Dems net about 3 House seats and 1 Senate seat in Fargo and Grand Forks. In D41, Heidenreich (D) leads by just 33 votes. The GOP keeps 2/3 supermajorities in both chambers (KFGO/North Dakota Monitor, Nov. 4).

Acton (D) beats Ramaswamy (R) for governor. The GOP loses its 3/5 House supermajority: Dems have at least 42 seats called and about 43 counting leads, and 4 races head to recounts, which cannot start until certification Nov. 24. The GOP keeps its Senate supermajority 22-11 (Ballotpedia News Nov. 8; Signal Cleveland Nov. 5; Bricker Nov. 4).

Mazzei (R) beats Munson (D) by about 6 points. Dems flip 6 GOP House seats (75-26) and lose none; HD64 (Suttles-D) was about 50-49. No Senate changes (40-8). The GOP keeps 2/3 supermajorities in both chambers but is 1 seat short of 3/4 in the House (HPPR Nov. 5; News 9; KOKH Nov. 4).

Kotek (D) reelected (AP). Dems are on track for a record 39 of 60 House seats and 19 of 30 Senate seats: above 3/5 for taxes but 1 seat short of 2/3 in each chamber (OPB, Oregon Capital Chronicle, Nov. 4).

Shapiro (D) reelected in a landslide. AP called the Senate for Dems 26-24 (they flipped 4 seats and lost 1), giving the first Dem trifecta since 1993. The House grows to about 112 of 203, counting Hayes' (D) lead in HD143. HD41 (Lancaster) is within about 30-40 votes and uncalled (Spotlight PA, Nov. 4 and Nov. 6-9; NSA).

Foulkes (D) elected governor (AP). The GOP falls to 2 senators and 8 representatives. Dems flip 2 Senate and 2 House seats (one from an independent), and independent Allan Fung takes a GOP House seat. Dems keep both supermajorities (Boston Globe, Nov. 5; WJAR, Nov. 6).

Dems flip 10 House seats, including Majority Leader Caskey's, ending the GOP's 2/3 House supermajority (79 of 124; 83 needed). The Senate is not up, and its GOP supermajority remains (WIS/WTOC Nov. 4; WCIV Nov. 4).

Rhoden (R) reelected with ~63.5%. Dems +5 House (5 to 10, mostly Sioux Falls) and -1 Senate (3 to 2); independent Evangeline Poor Bear (aligns with GOP) wins HD27. GOP keeps supermajorities, 59 of 70 House and 33 of 35 Senate (SD Searchlight via KFGO, Nov. 4; Fox News, Nov. 6).

Blackburn (R) elected, 45.5%-43.0% over Green (D), who conceded. Dems flip six GOP House seats (three in Rutherford Co.), 23 to 29 of 99; Senate unchanged 27-6. GOP keeps 2/3 in both (69 of 99, 27 of 33) (Tennessee Lookout/NewsChannel 5, Nov. 4; Fox 17, Nov. 8; Ballotpedia).

Hinojosa (D) unseats Abbott, and Dems flip the House, 62 to ~83 of 150 if leads hold (The Texan, Nov. 4). Of 6 GOP-held seats uncalled Nov. 9, Dems lead HD55 (+419, Hickland (R) conceded), HD14 (+315) and HD126 (+265). The GOP leads HD26 (+134), HD61 (+134) and HD67 (+203) (The Texan, Nov. 9). GOP keeps Senate 19-12 (AP via Fox 4, Nov. 4). Provisional ballots reviewed through Nov. 13.

GOP loses its House supermajority, held for at least 26 years: as of Nov. 9 Republicans lead 45 of 75 seats (50 needed), Dems 28 (from 14) and unaffiliated candidates 2. Dems flip 2 Senate seats, including ousting Majority Leader Cullimore. Forward Sen. Buss trails Benson (R) by 512, so the GOP keeps its Senate supermajority at ~21 of 29 (Utah News Dispatch, Fox 13, Nov. 9). Canvass Nov. 23.

Scott (R) wins a record 6th term, 52.6%-45.6% over Janoo (AP via Valley News, Nov. 5). Dems regain veto-proof supermajorities: House 102 of 150 (from 87; 100 needed) and Senate 20 of 30 (from 16; exactly the 2/3 line), plus Progressive and independent allies (Seven Days, Nov. 4). Unofficial; recounts likely in two House races (Hardwick R +8, southern Franklin D +2).

No legislative or governor elections in 2026 (Spanberger (D) elected 2025; House of Delegates up 2027, Senate 2027). Dems hold the House 63-36 with HD20 vacant, and the Senate 21-19; no supermajorities (Ballotpedia).

Dems win a two-thirds House supermajority, the first since 1949. AP has called 7 GOP-held seats for Dems (LDs 14, 17, 18 and Kitsap/LD26), giving at least 66 of 98 (KUOW, Nov. 9). Berg (D) leads Rep. Keaton (R) in LD25 by ~670; LD12 (Burnett, R, ~100 votes) and LD25 (Jacobsen, R, +~220) are still close (KIRO via Yahoo, Nov. 10). Dems flip 1 Senate seat for 31-18; no Senate supermajority (33 needed). Certification Dec. 3.

Dems more than double in the House of Delegates, 9 to 21 of 100 (12 gains, no losses reported), and go from 2 to 4 in the Senate (Jackson holds Woelfel's seat; Williams and Robb flip seats). Sen. Chapman (R) beats Del. Fluharty. GOP keeps supermajorities: ~79 of 100 and 30 of 34 (WV MetroNews, Nov. 3-4; WV Watch, Nov. 4).

Crowley (D) beats Tiffany (R) 54-46. Dems flip both chambers for the first trifecta since 2011: Assembly 53-46 (8 flips) and Senate 18-15 (flips in SDs 5, 17 and 21; Dems hold SD31) (WPR, Wisconsin Watch, Nov. 4).

Barlow (R) elected governor (AP call at poll close; WyoFile, Nov. 4). Dem Britney Tennant flips open Cheyenne HD11 by 54 votes, for 7 of 62 House seats; Senate stays 29-2. GOP keeps both supermajorities (Cowboy State Daily, Nov. 4; Brownstein, Nov. 4).
